<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[9] A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19503</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> In-Sung Park, Yongsup Park</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Jong-Am Hong, Min-Jae Maeng, Kyu-Myung Lee, Seunggu Lee, In-Sung Park, Yongsup Park</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 9/10</span> <b>A_MUST_READ</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> title strong match: photoemission</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#photoemission</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arxiv-logo-fb.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.</p></description>

      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20214</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Zhijin Li, Tinghong Shen</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>C_MAYBE</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical study using CFT and QMC to understand quantum criticality in 2D quantum magnets.; tier capped to C: formal/generic theory watch</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#quantumcriticality</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#quantummagnets</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theoreticalphysics</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#stronglycorrelatedelectrons</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2611.20214v1/bootstrap_global.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $\phi$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $\Delta_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[9] Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial -Sb on Al(111)</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.05424</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Yang Wang, Pujing Zhang</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 9/10</span> <b>A_MUST_READ</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Experimental STM/STS/photoemission study on emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial Sb.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#STM/STS</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#photoemission</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#kagome</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#electronicstructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#spinHall</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arxiv-logo-fb.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We report the epitaxial growth of $\beta$-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as $\beta$-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm. Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within $\beta$-Sb. For a reference $\beta$-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[7] Easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB2 at low temperatures</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20149</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Ulrich Zeitler, Christian Pfleiderer</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Christoph Resch, Georg Benka, Andreas Bauer, Elvina Dilmieva, Ulrich Zeitler, Christian Pfleiderer</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Experimental characterization of easy-plane ferromagnetism in single-crystal ErB2.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#material</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#magnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#ferromagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#characterization</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#transport</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2504.20149v2/figures/figure1-v1.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We report a study of high-quality single crystals of the hexagonal rare-earth diboride ErB$_{2}$ prepared by means of the self-adjusted flux travelling-solvent floating-zone technique.       <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Qiang-Hua Wang, Congjun Wu</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Da Wang, Qiang-Hua Wang, Congjun Wu</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory on nonreciprocal Shapiro steps in Josephson diodes, with implications for TRSB experiments.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#TRSB</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Josephsoneffect</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2506.23200v2/fig1.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Various microscopic mechanisms have been proposed for the Josephson diode effect, which are unified phenomenologically within a nonreciprocal resistively and capacitively shunted junction model. <item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[7] Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian (Annals of Physics)</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26128</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Klaus Ziegler</p><p><b>Published as:</b> Annals of Physics <a href='https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aop.2026.170837'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory on topological pseudospin order and edge modes in 2D superconductors, relevant to topological superconductivity.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topological</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#edgestates</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2510.26128v3/sc_ring.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.</p></description>

      <title>[9] Electric-field-controlled altermagnetic spin-momentum locking and ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance in Bilayer Cr2SeO</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23253</link>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[8] A Quantum Many-Body Approach for Orbital Magnetism in Correlated Multiband Electron Systems</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14372</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Mengxing Ye</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Advanced many-body theory for orbital magnetism and Berry curvature in correlated multiband electron systems.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#stronglycorrelated</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#orbitalmagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Berrycurvature</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Luttinger-Ward</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Orbital magnetism is a purely quantum phenomenon that reflects intrinsic electronic properties of solids, yet its microscopic description in interacting multiband systems remains incomplete. We develop a general quantum many-body framework for orbital magnetic responses based on the Luttinger--Ward functional. Starting from the Dyson equation, we reformulate the thermodynamic potential in a weak magnetic field and construct a controlled expansion in powers of $B$ applicable to correlated electron systems. A key technical advance is a modified ``Fourier'' representation using noncommutative coordinates, which allows the thermodynamic potential to be expressed in an effective momentum space where the magnetic field acts perturbatively. This formulation makes analytic progress possible within the Moyal algebra. As an application, we derive the spontaneous orbital magnetization for approximations whose skeleton diagrams contain no fermion loop enclosing magnetic flux (e.g., Hartree--Fock, self-consistent RPA, and single-site dynamical mean-field theory). Vertex corrections consistent with the self-energy are included automatically, without a separate diagrammatic analysis, and the result is expressed entirely in terms of the zero-field Hamiltonian renormalized by the self-energy. For frequency-dependent but Hermitian self-energies, we generalize the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature to momentum-frequency space and identify two gauge-invariant contributions built from these quantities. For frequency-independent self-energies the result reduces to the familiar geometric formula for noninteracting systems. This framework provides a unified foundation for computing orbital magnetic responses in correlated multiband materials.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">

      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.15131</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Vladimir P. Mineev</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory on band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb, directly relevant to electronic structure and altermagnetism.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#altermagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#bandstructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#CrSb</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2602.15131v4/Fig1.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by R.M.Fernandes et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.</p></description>

      <title>[9] Linear response of the Chern insulator MnBi2Te4: A Wannier function approach</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11268</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, J. E. Sipe</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Matthew Albert, Javier Sivianes, Jason G. Kattan, Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, J. E. Belashchenko</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical study of surface altermagnetism in antiferromagnets, relevant for transport and experimental probes.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#altermagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#antiferromagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#surface</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#transport</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting.       <title>[8] Valley-controlled chiral magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02260</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Igor S. Krivenko, Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical study of valley-controlled chiral magnetism and RKKY in TMD monolayers, relevant to 2D materials and QSLs.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#monolayer</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#TMD</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#vanderWaals</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#heterostructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#magnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#RKKY</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#quantumspinliquid</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2608.02260v2/RKKY3.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. Using mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this interaction qualitatively reshapes the phase diagram of atomically thin antiferromagnets. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.</p></description>

Smirnov</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical study of valley-controlled chiral magnetism and RKKY in TMD monolayers, relevant to 2D materials and QSLs.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#monolayer</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#TMD</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#vanderWaals</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#heterostructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#magnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#RKKY</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#quantumspinliquid</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2608.02260v2/RKKY3.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.</p></content:encoded></item>

      <title>[7] Kinetic Lifshitz invariants and dynamics of nonreciprocal fluctuations in superconductors</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05306</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Tony Liu, Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical study of nonreciprocal effects and diode efficiency in noncentrosymmetric Rashba superconductors.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#noncentrosymmetric</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#RashbaSOC</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#transport</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Ginzburg-Landau</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We derive the generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory of a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, using a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field as a minimal model. The couplings of the quadratic sector are governed by a single closed-form kernel controlled by the ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate to temperature. It interpolates between the weak-relaxation regime, where the invariants are suppressed, and the relaxation-dominated regime, where the helical modulation of the order parameter saturates at a universal, disorder-independent value. This crossover reconciles known results for the magnetoelectric couplings of disordered Rashba superconductors. Because the theory is formulated on the Keldysh contour, it also determines the dissipative dynamics: the relaxation rate of a fluctuation with pair momentum $q$, and hence the Langevin noise power, acquires a term odd in $q$ and odd in the magnetic field. The structure of this kinetic Lifshitz invariant is dictated by Onsager reciprocity: friction and noise change together, so that equal-time fluctuations remain Gibbsian while the relaxation dynamics becomes nonreciprocal. As applications we compute the superconducting diode efficiency near $T_c$, where the cubic invariant competes with the quartic vertex and with higher-gradient terms, reversing the sign of the diode coefficient. We also consider fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy above $T_c$, which grows as the inverse square of the distance to $T_c$ and is suppressed in the relaxation-dominated regime.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">

      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18382</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Kenji Watanabe, Feng Wang</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Ha-Leem Kim, Hyungbin Lim, Yuanyi Yang, et al.</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Experimental technique for spatially resolved transport in 2D semiconductors and vdW heterostructures, relevant to correlated states.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#experimentaltechnique</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#2Dmaterials</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#vanderWaals</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#transport</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#correlatedelectrons</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arxiv-logo-fb.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. <item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[8] Spin-current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in p-wave antialtermagnets</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03075</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Kristian M{\ae}land, Bj\"orn Trauzettel</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory on spin-current effects in p-wave antialtermagnets, a directly relevant topic for the user.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#altermagnetism</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#magnons</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#spincurrent</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2609.03075v2/contour.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We show that $p$-wave magnetic insulators efficiently generate magnetization via a linear thermal magnon Edelstein effect. Furthermore, they can generate perfectly nonreciprocal spin currents through a purely even-order nonlinear response. This makes them promising candidates for spin-current rectification. More generally, we find that odd-parity-wave magnets with coplanar ground states host magnons with zero magnetic moment in the plane. Instead the magnons carry a colinear, out-of-plane magnetic moment, placing coplanar odd-parity-wave magnets within the class of antialtermagnets. We establish these general results using symmetry arguments and demonstrate them explicitly for a two-dimensional model with a coplanar ground state containing the minimal number of sublattices, inspired by the ground state of CeNiAsO. Our conclusions hold both in the absence and in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.</p></description>

      <title>[7] When the electrons go marching in: Resonances and accuracy of pairwise approximations in multiterminal Josephson junctions</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40346</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> A. Bar{\i}\c{s} \"Ozg\"uler</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theoretical analysis of multiterminal Josephson junctions, relevant to superconductivity and quantum devices.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#superconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Josephsonjunctions</span></p><p><img src='data:image/png;base64,' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Multiterminal Josephson junctions connect three or more superconductors through a common weak link. We quantify when their equilibrium currents admit a pairwise description. Multiterminal irreducible harmonics are energy components that depend jointly on three or more terminal phases and cannot be reduced to a sum of pair couplings. In microscopic planar-junction models, pairwise terms can capture nearly all energy variation while leaving appreciable current errors: phase differentiation amplifies the omitted harmonics. A terminal-independent Fourier projection quantifies this effect while allowing arbitrary nonsinusoidal pair couplings. Shared normal-region resonances provide a means of controlling the error. Selecting a mode from normal-state data and shifting it with a gate while retaining a frozen background reproduces the normalized error trends in the tested devices; prediction of the complete current waveform also depends on the background contribution. Finite-gap calculations retain the gate dependence at substantially lower absolute currents. An analytic single-level model supplies a sufficient detuning for pairwise accuracy. Together, these results connect normal-resonance control to a quantitative, current-based criterion for pairwise modeling.</p></description>

      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, et al.</p><p><b>Published as:</b> J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. <a href='https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.95.123701'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 9/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Experimental NQR study of spin-stripe SDW order in nickelate La3Ni2O7, directly relevant to unconventional superconductivity.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#experimental</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#unconventionalsuperconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#nickelates</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#SDW</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#NQR</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#stronglycorrelatedelectrons</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2610.20446v3/fig1.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.</p></description>

Jpn. <a href='https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.95.123701'>DOI</a></p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 9/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Experimental NQR study of spin-stripe SDW order in nickelate La3Ni2O7, directly relevant to unconventional superconductivity.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#experimental</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#unconventionalsuperconductivity</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#nickelates</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#SDW</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#NQR</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#stronglycorrelatedelectrons</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2610.20446v3/fig1.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure.       <title>[8] Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04996</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Directly relevant to topological semimetals and Berry curvature with proposed experimental nonlinear Hall signatures.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Diracsemimetal</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topology</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2611.04996v2/fig1a.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.</p></description>

<item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[8] Raman optical activity and helicity-dependent phonon splitting in chiral CoSi</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06909</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Yoshihiko Togawa, Takuya Satoh</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Kohei Miyazaki, et al.</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 8/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Investigates structural chirality and phonons in topological semimetal CoSi using helicity-dependent Raman scattering.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#CoSi</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topologicalsemimetal</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#Raman</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#chiralphonons</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2606.06909v2/CoSi_struc.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Circularly polarized Raman scattering in solids provides access to two distinct phenomena: Raman optical activity (ROA), an intensity difference between circular polarization channels, and helicity-dependent frequency splitting of chiral phonons. We observe both in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi and show that they arise through two different symmetry channels, each rendering phonon components with opposite crystal angular momenta inequivalent. Doubly degenerate E phonons exhibit a large ROA, with an approximately fourfold intensity contrast between the two cross-circular channels. The sign of this ROA reverses between the front and back {111} surfaces, while its strong suppression on {110} supports the assignment to the axial electric toroidal octupole. By contrast, triply degenerate T phonons show helicity-dependent frequency splittings, whose mode-dependent signs are reproduced by the calculated dispersion of branches with opposite crystal angular momenta, thus identifying structural chirality as their source. These results establish circularly polarized Raman scattering as a symmetry- and angular-momentum-resolved probe of chiral and axial multipolar symmetry in solids.</p></description>

The magnetic phases are determined using self-consistent mean-field calculations. We first consider a single crystal-field doublet with exchange and polar-type Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. We find square skyrmion lattices with distinct magnetic periods, as well as a rectangular skyrmion lattice that spontaneously breaks the in-plane fourfold rotational symmetry. Their stability and field-induced phase sequences are strongly controlled by the crystal-field wave function, including reentrant behavior of the rectangular phase. Second-neighbor exchange further modifies the competition among these states. When a second crystal-field doublet is retained, additional rectangular skyrmion lattices with distinct modulation patterns emerge, together with axial single-$Q$ states and various double-$Q$ states. <item xmlns:arxiv="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:content="http://purl.org/rss/1.0/modules/content/">
      <title>[7] A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth</title>
      <link>https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21244</link>
      <description><p><b>Last authors:</b> Nir Goldman, Ben Hourahine</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Method for topological materials discovery in heavy-element systems like bismuth.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#topological</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#electronicstructure</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#bismuth</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/html/2611.21244v1/figures/structures/rhombohedral_bi_primitive.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.</p></description>

Louie</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, et al.</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory of exciton magnetic moment in bilayer graphene, connects to quantum geometry and experiment.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#graphene</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#quantumgeometry</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#magnetism</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arxiv-logo-fb.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our formalism reveals three distinct contributions that go beyond the heuristic approaches used in the literature: a Berry-phase-corrected single-particle electron and hole moment difference, a term from envelope-function winding linked to electron-hole relative motion, and a center-of-mass correction from exciton band quantum geometry, with the latter two being completely new effects not considered in previous studies. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.</p></description>

Louie</p><p><b>Authors:</b> Gurjyot Sethi, Jiawei Ruan, Fang Zhang, et al.</p><p><span style='display:inline-block;padding:4px 9px;border-radius:999px;background:#fee2e2;color:#991b1b;font-weight:700;'>Score 7/10</span> <b>B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT</b></p><p><b>Why:</b> Theory of exciton magnetic moment in bilayer graphene, connects to quantum geometry and experiment.</p><p><b>Tags:</b> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#theory</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#graphene</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#quantumgeometry</span> <span style='display:inline-block;margin:2px 4px 2px 0;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:999px;background:#eef2ff;color:#3730a3;font-size:12px;'>#magnetism</span></p><p><img src='https://arxiv.org/static/browse/0.3.4/images/arxiv-logo-fb.png' style='max-width:100%;height:auto;border-radius:10px;' /></p><hr/><p><b>Abstract:</b> Combining magnetometry with optical spectroscopy has uncovered novel quantum phenomena and is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum materials. However, the theory of the magnetic response of excitons, correlated electron-hole pairs in insulators, remains incomplete due to insufficient treatment of electron-hole interactions and quantum geometric effects. In biased bilayer graphene, for instance, theoretical predictions of valley g-factors for p-excitons deviate from experiment by nearly an order of magnitude. Here, we develop a quantum theory of the exciton orbital magnetic moment, based on first-order perturbation theory within the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter Equation approach and a rigorous treatment of the position operator in the response of exciton states to a magnetic field. Our ab initio calculations yield results in excellent agreement with experiment, establishing the importance of interaction and quantum geometric effects in the magnetic response of excitons.</p></content:encoded></item>

Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5 %, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of point defects (Spearman $\rho$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($\rho$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($\rho$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %.</p></content:encoded></item>
